item.text:
# Joko Widodo, 2024, 2B.9 Research Note

Assessment: **negative overall**. I found credible evidence of serious civilian harm and weak accountability in Papua, plus only a narrow institutional acknowledgment by the military after torture footage circulated. I did **not** find clear 2024 evidence that Jokowi himself accepted responsibility for military failures or for later evidence contradicting the state’s justifications.

| Valence | Title | Publisher / date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mixed / partial | [2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Indonesia](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html) | U.S. Department of State, published 2025-08-12; report covers 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html | The report says the government did not systematically take credible steps to identify and punish officials who committed abuses. It also notes that TNI apologized and detained 13 soldiers after torture videos surfaced, but police and military often failed to investigate or disclose findings. This is the closest 2024 accountability evidence, but it is institutional and incomplete, not clear presidential acceptance of responsibility. | `2B.9`, `2B.4` |
| Negative | [Human Rights Committee finds Indonesia still failing to investigate Papuan abuses](https://www.unognewsroom.org/teleprompter/en/2120/ohchr-press-conference-un-human-rights-committees-findings-28-march-2024/6411) | OHCHR / UNOG, 2024-03-28 | https://www.unognewsroom.org/teleprompter/en/2120/ohchr-press-conference-un-human-rights-committees-findings-28-march-2024/6411 | The UN Human Rights Committee said it remained concerned by multiple reports of extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances of indigenous people in Papua that had not been investigated. That directly points to a failure to accept accountability for abuse. | `2B.9`, `2B.4` |
| Negative | [“If It’s Not Racism, What Is It?”: Discrimination and Other Abuses Against Papuans in Indonesia](https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-its-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in) | Human Rights Watch, 2024-09-18 | https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-it-s-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in | HRW says Indonesian security forces committed arbitrary arrests, torture, extrajudicial killings, and mass forced displacement in Papua and were seldom held to account. The report specifically calls for accountability, which implies the existing response was inadequate. | `2B.9`, `2B.4` |
| Negative / corroborative | [Annual Report 2024: Human Rights and Conflict in West Papua](https://humanrightsmonitor.org/reports/annual-report-2024-human-rights-and-conflict-in-west-papua/) | Human Rights Monitor, 2024 | https://humanrightsmonitor.org/reports/annual-report-2024-human-rights-and-conflict-in-west-papua/ | HRM reports no public trials resulting from police or military abuse cases in 2024, with opaque internal investigations and weak punishment. It also says misinformation about alleged abuses was used to blunt accountability pressure. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.6` |

## Synthesis

- The clearest pattern is **weak accountability** for security-force abuses in Papua.
- I found **one partial institutional response**: the military apologized and detained soldiers after torture footage circulated.
- I did **not** find evidence that Jokowi personally acknowledged fault, changed the stated justification after contrary evidence emerged, or publicly accepted responsibility for military abuses.

## Search gap

The 2024 record is strongest on **abuse and non-accountability in Papua**, not on presidential admissions. If you want a stricter ruler-level verdict, the missing piece is direct evidence of Jokowi personally taking responsibility for those failures.
